title: Guard bytes
description:
Catch buffer overruns by surrounding each allocation with known bytes.

```
alloc 16 bytes -> [guard 8][16 bytes][guard 8]
write 16 bytes: fine
write 17 bytes: overrun detected when freed (guard after block damaged)
```
hints: Layout: `[size_t size][guard bytes][user bytes][guard bytes]`; return the address of the user bytes (lesson 6.05).
Keep the size field aligned (put it first, as a `std::size_t`) so the user block is aligned too.
requirements: `void* guardedAlloc(std::size_t)` reserves extra bytes before and after, fills them with `0xFD`, and stores the size.
`guardedFree(void*)` checks both guards, reports damage, then frees.
Show one correct use and one off-by-one write.
stretch: Fill freed memory with `0xDD` too, so use-after-free shows up as strange values.
